themes.label: Mag7 unwind is rotation, not rollover — yet
themes.narrative: The tape reads like a broad market rollover: QQQ is down 6.64% in a month and 3.16% on the day, and GOOGL sits 31.5% below its 52-week high. The Mag7-led selloff is being priced as the start of a general unwind.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 3.3% below its 52-week high against a Mag7 average of 16.0% below theirs — a 12.7-point divergence gap — and the index itself is down just 0.9% over one month. Credit is not confirming a rollover: HY OAS is 3.26, well inside calm territory, and bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). AAPL, the strongest Mag7 name, is only 2% off its high.
themes.counterRead: The rollover narrative runs ahead of the credit data, so extrapolating Mag7 weakness into a broad crash is premature — but the divergence is real and credit conditions can flip. If HY OAS pushes toward 4% or the SPY gap closes from the index side rather than the Mag7 side, the read changes to rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SPY's distance from its 52-week high widening past 8% while Mag7 stays flat.

themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price, no floor yet
themes.narrative: The market now prices AI infrastructure as a financing trade that has broken: SMH fell 6.98% in a day and sits 22.23% below its 120-day high, NVDA is down 11.09% in a month, and the FOMC event signal is HIGH with headlines about the Fed signalling higher rates. The story is that the capex cycle cannot fund itself at a 10-year yield of 4.98%.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data has not broken: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY, AVGO 55% YoY, LRCX 131.3% YoY, and AMAT 11.4% YoY — all while their stocks sit 15.9%, 34.1%, 45.5% and 47.3% below 52-week highs. AVGO carries the top conviction score (81, tier A) on a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% FCF margin. NVDA is already inside Zone 1 ($200-210) at $204.64.
themes.counterRead: Fundamentals are ahead of price, which is the opportunity setup — but price has no floor: SMH is between zones at $522.49 with its 50-day at $572.62 still 8.75% above, NVDA sits 0.12% above its 200-day, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4 (no volume-climax reversal, no VIX rollover). Buying into the gap between data and price before a zone print or a capitulation signal is catching a falling multiple, not buying a bottom.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing into Zone 2 ($470-505) or NVDA into Zone 2 ($175-185) with the capitulation tally reaching 3 of 4.

themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the demand story ran past near-term data
themes.narrative: AI power demand was priced as a supercycle: nuclear and power names were bid as the physical bottleneck of the AI buildout. That story has now reversed into a washout, with the whole complex down double digits in a month.
themes.dataAnchor: SMR is down 27.73% in one month and 65%+ names in the complex are deep off highs: OKLO -30.02% in a month, URA -14.12%, CCJ -10.21%, GEV -12.87%, VST 29.7% below its high. The dislocation list flags these as sentiment-driven, not earnings-driven. The one hard-data counterweight is insider: VST insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and VST's conviction score is 78.
themes.counterRead: The power-demand narrative was ahead of the price reality — the correction is the story repricing to what near-term data supports. VST's insider buying and its Level-1 supplier status to nuclear power argue the theme is not dead, but VST's own revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING, so the insider signal is a watch item, not a buy trigger.
themes.watchFor: VST revenue inflection flipping from DETERIORATING to RECOVERY, or SMR/OKLO stabilising above their October lows with volume drying up.

themes.label: Software / SaaS: oversold washout against intact growth
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is being sold as the AI loser — displaced by models, squeezed on seat pricing, and derated across the board. RDDT fell 28.86% in a day and 38.34% in a month; NOW is 43% below its high; APP is 69% below its high.
themes.dataAnchor: RSI readings are washed out — RDDT 17.5, GOOGL 21.4, APP 25.0, NOW 26.9, TER 28.8 — while the growth data holds: APP revenue growing 55.8% YoY with a 76% gross margin and 60.8% FCF margin, DDOG growing 34% YoY with an 80% gross margin, NOW flagged FULL_SIGNAL on sentiment, not fundamentals. DDOG scores 78 and APP 79 on conviction, both tier B.
themes.counterRead: Fundamentals are ahead of price by a wide margin, which is the classic dislocation setup — but oversold is not a floor, and the dislocation list classifies nearly all of these declines as SENTIMENT_DRIVEN with no catalyst to reverse them. The entry is a staged probe only after a print, never a chase of the first green day.
themes.watchFor: A bullish RSI divergence print or a close back above the 20-day average on APP, DDOG or NOW with volume above the 20-day average.

themes.label: Rates are the constraint, credit is the tripwire
themes.narrative: The Fed is signalling higher rates — the FOMC Oct 27-28 event is active with HIGH signal strength — and the 10-year sits at 4.98% with the 30-year at 5.32%. The market reads this as the ceiling on any equity recovery.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve is not inverted (2s10s +0.37), the real 10-year is 2.64%, and HY OAS at 3.26 is calm — credit is not cracking. VIX at 19.42 is up 12.91% on the day and 18.49% in a month, but it has not spiked into panic territory and has not rolled over (5-day high is 19.42 itself). The December FOMC (Dec 8-9) is already anticipated with HIGH signal strength, and midterms on Nov 3 are a watch event with 10 headline hits.
themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree: rates are the binding constraint and credit is the tripwire, not the trigger — yet. The alignment breaks if HY OAS moves toward 4% while the 10-year stays near 5%, which would turn a rate headwind into a credit event.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or the 10-year breaking above 5.2% while VIX holds above 25.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real (SPX -3.37% from its 120-day high, below its 50-day) but unconfirmed as a bottom: NVDA is in Zone 1 and the tally is only 2 of 4, with no volume-climax reversal and no VIX rollover. No new deployment until Zone 2 prints or a confirmed bottom forms.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex: SMH at $522.49 sits between Zone 1 ($540-565) and Zone 2 ($470-505), and NVDA is already in Zone 1 at $204.64. The trigger is either a Zone 2 print with the capitulation tally reaching 3 of 4, or a failed bounce into the SMH $580-600 failure zone that confirms the trap.

Mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 — zone occupancy and credit calm confirmed, volume climax and VIX rollover not. Episode data is fresh, not stale.

ladder.response: Stand down: regime break — void the ladder, halt all probe/add plans, and re-audit zones before any new deployment.

reaction.invalidation: A credit event — HY OAS above 4% with a second AI borrower cracking — or an SPX close below the 200-day at $7,309.76 proves the Watch stance wrong and voids the ladder; the episode would no longer be a correction to buy but a regime break to stand down from.
reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail risk is live: SMH is 8.75% below its 50-day and any sharp bounce toward the $580-600 failure zone is the bull trap until it holds above it. Do not chase the first bounce — entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict or a Zone 2 print with tally confirmation; a bounce that fails at $580-600 confirms the trap and keeps the stance at Watch.
